questions.prompt: Two VNets are peered and use Azure-provided DNS. A private zone contains a verified A record for db.corp.example and has a completed link only to vnet-a. A VM in vnet-a resolves it, but a VM in vnet-b cannot. Which change gives vnet-b access to the existing zone records?

options.text: Add a resolution-only link from the existing private zone to vnet-b.
options.explanation: The client VNet needs its own zone link with Azure-provided DNS. Autoregistration is unnecessary to resolve existing records.

options.text: Enable autoregistration on the existing link to vnet-a.
options.explanation: This registers vnet-a VM names; it does not link vnet-b to the zone.

options.text: Recreate the peering between the VNets without changing zone links.
options.explanation: Peering supplies network connectivity, not a private-zone link for vnet-b.

options.text: Create an empty second private zone and link only that zone to vnet-b.
options.explanation: An empty separate zone does not expose the verified record in the existing zone.

questions.prompt: You link a VNet to a private zone with autoregistration disabled. What does this link provide?

options.text: Automatic registration of every VM name.
Resolution of records in the linked zone without automatic VM registration.
Public Internet resolution of the zone.
Automatic VNet peering to all other linked networks.
options.explanation: DNS links do not create network peerings.

questions.prompt: A VNet using Azure-provided DNS has a completed link to alpha.example with autoregistration enabled. It must also resolve existing private records in beta.example while continuing to register its VM names only in alpha.example. Which final link configuration meets the requirements?

options.text: Keep alpha autoregistration enabled; add beta with autoregistration enabled.
options.explanation: A VNet can have only one registration zone. Two enabled registration links are not supported.

options.text: Disable alpha autoregistration; add beta with autoregistration disabled.
options.explanation: Both zones can resolve, but this stops the required VM-name registration in alpha.

options.text: Keep alpha autoregistration enabled; add beta with autoregistration disabled.
options.explanation: The existing registration zone remains alpha; the additional resolution-only link supplies beta lookups.

options.text: Disable alpha autoregistration; add beta with autoregistration enabled.
options.explanation: This moves registration to beta, contrary to the requirement to keep it only in alpha.
